newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: AUSTRIAN BONDS STEADY, BOOSTED BY DOLLAR LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRIAN BONDS STEADY, BOOSTED BY DOLLAR LOSSES.

text.p: Austrian bonds clawed back ground from earlier losses to end stable on Friday amid meagre turnover.
Traders said dollar weakness helped the market. Comments by German Bundesbank's Ernst Welteke that the economic situation did not allow for any rate hikes also gave support to the market.
However, the outlook for next week was not expected to be bullish, traders said. "The markets will remain nervous," said one. Today's dollar weakness is seen as temporary.
* 10-year benchmark 5.625 pct bond maturing July 2007 steady at 99.15 to yield 5.74 pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.04/12 to yield 5.75/74 pct.
* Five-year 4.625 bond maturing May 2002 stable at 99.25 to yield 4.80 pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.35/45 to yield 4.78/75 percent.
* Austrian bond future up one bp at 109.16.
* 10-year spread over Germany steady at seven bps, five-year lower at 18.
* Money market rates three-month VIBOR unchanged at 3.450 and overnight money at 3.11/3.36. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
